reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis incorrectly predicts that high-temperature salt exposure (700–900 °C) will be more protective than room-temperature exposure for Q235 steel, contradicting the well-known phenomenon of hot corrosion where molten salts aggressively attack and destroy protective oxides.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with well-defined measurements and a decisive falsification criterion, though the baseline comparison is slightly misaligned with the stated hypothesis.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it is based on a fundamental misunderstanding of hot corrosion mechanisms, and testing it would not advance understanding of corrosion protection in Q235 steel.
